prediction_ref.short_label: Consumer-GPU coding agents displace cloud-only APIs for 30% of devs

validation_rows.evidence_summary: [REVIVED] Layer-1 keyword + Layer-2 semantic match against the dormant snapshot's signals (local-first toggle, consumer-GPU coding agent, Ollama/MLX, hybrid harness, M5 Max, cloud-only API). Today's Kimi Work is a downloadable desktop coding/automation agent for Apple silicon and Windows that runs against the open-weight Kimi K2.6 - and the launch coverage stresses that the same K2.6 weights already run on-device through Unsloth's 2-bit (UD-Q2_K_XL) dynamic quantization, the consumer-and-workstation local-inference path the dormant prediction names. That is a concrete local-first agent operating on the user's own machine, files and browser session as a direct alternative to a cloud-only API, which is exactly the displacement dynamic the prediction tracks; the same-day Ona acquisition is the cloud-side counterweight, sharpening the local-vs-cloud line. The divergences are that Kimi Work is a general desktop worker rather than a coding-only agent and the launch reports no developer-share figure, so it revives and reinforces the consumer-hardware-agent thesis without quantifying the 30%-of-devs marker.

bridge.narrative: Kimi Work ships a downloadable desktop agent driving the user's own machine, files and browser on open-weight K2.6, runnable locally via Unsloth 2-bit quantization - a concrete local-first substitute for a cloud-only API, the displacement mechanism this thesis names. The same-day Ona cloud-sandbox deal sharpens that local-versus-cloud contest.
bridge.remaining_gap: Kimi Work is a general desktop worker, not a coding-only agent, and the launch reports no developer-adoption figure to anchor the 30%-of-devs threshold.

prediction_ref.short_label: SEC publishes AI compute prebuy disclosure concept release by Q1 2027

validation_rows.evidence_summary: [REVIVED] Layer-1 keyword match against the dormant snapshot's signals (SpaceX S-1, SpaceX roadshow $75B raise, SPCX pricing June 11 first trade June 12, Anthropic monthly compute fee, Oracle OCI, multi-year AI compute prebuy commitments). Today's news lands two of those signals directly: SpaceX officially priced its IPO on June 11 at $135 for about a $75B raise under SPCX, and OpenAI and Oracle moved to let Oracle Cloud customers apply Universal Credits toward OpenAI's frontier models and Codex - an incumbent-cloud compute-commitment channel. The dormant thesis is that the SEC issues a concept release on how multi-year AI compute prebuy commitments (committed compute revenue versus cancellable capacity leases) should be disclosed, with the SpaceX S-1 and large lab-cloud compute deals as the catalyst. Today's SPCX pricing and the Oracle credit-routing arrangement keep that compute-commitment-disclosure backdrop live and concrete. The match is on the catalysts, not the outcome: there is no SEC Division of Corporation Finance action today, so this revives the disclosure-pressure thesis on fresh prebuy/IPO signals without movement on the regulatory landing itself.

validation_rows.evidence_summary: [REVIVED] Layer-1 keyword + Layer-2 semantic match against the dormant snapshot's signals (on-prem inference, VRAM floor, local-LLM standard, single high-end GPU, on-device). Today's Zyphra Zamba2-VL ships open weights at 1.2B/2.7B/7B under Apache 2.0 explicitly sized for local hardware, pitching roughly an order-of-magnitude lower time-to-first-token for on-device document and screen understanding - the local-inference envelope the dormant prediction describes. It revives the broad thesis that capable open models are converging on a single-machine, local-deployment standard rather than API-only endpoints. But it diverges sharply from the specific marker on every concrete axis: the family is 1-7B not 27B, the backbone is a Mamba2 state-space hybrid rather than dense transformer, the context is 32K-class prefill rather than 1M, and it is multimodal vision-language rather than the text local-LLM the prediction names - so it is a low-relevance revival of the local-standard direction, not a match to the 27B-dense/1M-context specification.

It only touches that direction loosely, not the prediction's specific configuration.
bridge.remaining_gap: Diverges on every concrete axis: 1-7B not 27B, Mamba2 hybrid not dense transformer, 32K-class not 1M context, and vision-language rather than a text local-LLM.
